alerts.reason: December net sales grew 0.6% as a 12.0% increase in average unit price offset a 10.0% decline in units (A, B, D). I expect pricing to keep March sales growth above -5%, then provide less protection in April–June. With units still down 10%, even a 5% price increase would imply a sales decline of about 5.5%.

December net product sales fell 2.1%, leaving 2.9 percentage points to the threshold (A). Lower volumes drove both the quarterly and annual declines, and customers and consumers were increasingly resistant to higher prices (B, D). I expect the March decline to stay under 5% and further volume losses to take the April–June decline to at least 5%.

Astec's 2024 net sales fell 2.5%, while year-end orders in backlog fell 26.4%, from $569.8 million to $419.6 million (A, C). I expect existing orders to cushion March sales enough to keep the decline under 5%, with fewer orders left to ship in April–June pushing the decline to at least 5%.

CSX's 2024 total revenue fell 1%. Merchandise pricing gains and higher merchandise and intermodal volumes partly offset lower fuel recovery and coal revenue. Trucking surcharges also fell (A–C). I expect those offsets to keep the March decline under 5%, then weaken enough for coal and surcharge losses to push the April–June decline to at least 5%.

Schneider's reported 2024 revenue fell about 4%. Lower brokerage volume and revenue per order cut Logistics revenue excluding fuel surcharges by $112.4 million even with Cowan's contribution. Network rates and volumes and Intermodal revenue per order also fell (A, B, E). I expect the acquisition contribution to help keep March above -5%, with pressure across those businesses taking reported April–June revenue growth to -5% or lower.
